extraction.notes: Research-note claims extracted as UNVERIFIED; document explicitly is not binding architecture.

claims.normalized_claim: The research goal is not to recover historically true hidden 3D geometry from one image but to construct plausible closed editable walkable synthetic geometry consistent with the visible projection.
claims.subject: synthetic-reconstruction

claims.normalized_claim: The cheapest solver may deliberately use strong priors such as planes, Manhattan geometry, shared ground and vertical axes, closed volumes and synthetic hidden faces.
claims.subject: synthetic-reconstruction

claims.normalized_claim: The proposed alternative to depth-first reconstruction is structure-first: detect faces, edges and relations, rectify perspective, build a face graph, fold local volumes and place them globally.
claims.subject: structure-first

claims.normalized_claim: Global vanishing-direction families should be fitted from structural lines rather than inventing a new vanishing point per edge or object.
claims.subject: vanishing-points

claims.normalized_claim: Topological relations and direction families are treated as hard constraints while exact pixel corner positions are soft observations.
claims.subject: constraints

claims.normalized_claim: Detected planar surfaces can be perspective-rectified and then used directly as mesh faces and texture-bearing construction elements.
claims.subject: faces

claims.normalized_claim: Inverse papercraft is proposed as a model: visible rectified faces plus shared edges and fold relations can be assembled into 3D geometry.
claims.subject: inverse-papercraft

claims.normalized_claim: For simple architecture, hidden geometry can be synthesized by parallel copying, mirroring or translating visible opposite faces to close a volume.
claims.subject: completion

claims.normalized_claim: Success for synthetic hidden geometry is defined by closure, consistency, editability, walkability, textureability and extensibility rather than ground-truth recovery.
claims.subject: success-metric

claims.normalized_claim: Local GROW, ERODE and SMOOTH operators were found prone to contour tracing or noisy emergent patterns when driven only by image energy.
claims.subject: cellular-operators

claims.normalized_claim: A boundary-walker agent can trace structural edges using heading, inside-side, direction-family and visited state, leaving a graph behind.
claims.subject: boundary-walker

claims.normalized_claim: A surface cultivator can grow seeded regions until structurally plausible boundaries or other regions are reached, allowing shared boundaries to emerge without separately detecting every edge.
claims.subject: surface-cultivator

claims.normalized_claim: The Piazza principle treats local measurements as soft but topology, orthogonality and loop closure as hard global constraints used to correct accumulated local error.
claims.subject: global-constraints

claims.normalized_claim: Multiple scene objects can constrain one another through shared camera, ground plane, vertical axis, direction families and occlusion ordering.
claims.subject: multi-object
